public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 666

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/666](https://www.erdosproblems.com/666)
- [BDT93] Brouwer, A. E. and Dejter, I. J. and Thomassen, C., *Highly symmetric subgraphs of
  hypercubes*. J. Algebraic Combin. (1993), 25-29.
- [Ch92] Chung, Fan R. K., *Subgraphs of a hypercube containing no small even cycles*. J. Graph
  Theory (1992), 273-286.
- [Er91] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number
  theory*. Graph theory, combinatorics, and applications, Vol. 1 (Kalamazoo, MI, 1988) (1991),
  397-406.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter SimpleGraph

open scoped Finset

namespace Erdos666

/--
Let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube graph (so that $Q_n$ has $2^n$ vertices and $n2^{n-1}$
edges). Is it true that, for every $\epsilon>0$, if $n$ is sufficiently large, every subgraph of
$Q_n$ with
$$\geq \epsilon  n2^{n-1}$$
many edges contains a $C_6$?

The answer to this problem is no: Chung [Ch92] and Brouwer, Dejter, and Thomassen [BDT93]
constructed an edge-partition of $Q_n$ into four subgraphs, each containing no $C_6$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos666.lean"]
theorem erdos_666 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ H : SimpleGraph (Fin n → Bool), H ≤ hypercube n →
      ε * n * 2 ^ (n - 1 : ℕ) ≤ (H.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) → (cycleGraph 6 ⊑ H) := by
  sorry

end Erdos666

reformulations.difference: Lean quantifies over spanning graphs H on Fin n → Bool with H ≤ hypercube n, whereas the source permits arbitrary subgraphs. It also expresses sufficiently large n using eventuality at atTop.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An arbitrary subgraph K can be extended to all hypercube vertices by adding isolated vertices. Its edge set is unchanged, and adding isolated vertices neither creates nor destroys a copy of C₆, since every C₆ vertex has an incident edge. Conversely, every H ≤ hypercube n determines a spanning subgraph. Eventuality at atTop on ℕ is exactly ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N. The full equivalence with explicit thresholds and arbitrary SimpleGraph.Subgraph objects was proved as source_quantification_equivalent in /workspace/review/scratch.lean; its axioms are only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.

review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states the source's negative answer, and the solved/formal-proof status agrees with the source. Checked undirected edge counting, non-induced cycle containment, quantifier scope, real coercions, and small dimensions. Lean computations confirmed hypercube vertex and edge counts for n = 0,…,6; additional proofs checked cycle containment, finite edge sets, satisfiable density hypotheses, and the irrelevance of small dimensions to eventuality. The full [Er91] chapter was not retrieved, but the main question and counterexample are corroborated by the problem page, [Ch92], and [BDT93]. The linked external theorem is equivalent under Bool ≃ ZMod 2 and the cycle-containment characterization; its source contains no sorry, admit, or custom axioms. Its original 4.29.1 toolchain was unavailable, and compilation against the sandbox's 4.33.1 encounters API incompatibilities, so no fresh kernel verification of that external proof is claimed.
